title: Unauthenticated tool-management API gives arbitrary code execution
failure_scenario: Any client that can reach :8000 -> POST /api/tools (create a Python/Node tool, no key) -> POST /api/tools/{name}/run -> the saved script runs as a subprocess in the app container. No Authorization is checked on any /api/* route (only POST /mcp is gated). Create+run == shell in the container.
evidence: Against the local WSL instance with OMNIFORGE_API_KEY set, with NO Authorization header: POST /api/tools returned 200 and created tools; POST /api/tools/{name}/run executed them (exit_code 0, stdout returned). _check_api_key is referenced only by POST /mcp (main.py:196); dashboard (82), api_config (88), api_list_tools, api_create_tool (113), api_update/delete (138), api_toggle, api_run_tool (169) call it nowhere.
suggested_fix: Require the same bearer check on all state-changing and data routes (or put the whole app behind auth/reverse proxy). At minimum gate POST/PUT/DELETE /api/tools* and /run identically to POST /mcp.
exposure_note: LAN: high - any LAN host/process (or a browser driven cross-origin, see SEC-03) gets RCE; container hardening bounds blast radius to the container. Exposed/tunnelled: critical - unauthenticated internet RCE.

title: Scripts inherit full app environment incl. OMNIFORGE_API_KEY and can read/modify the DB and all tool code
failure_scenario: A tool script (reachable via SEC-01 or an MCP key) runs with os.environ.copy(), so it reads OMNIFORGE_API_KEY (the server's own MCP bearer key) and OMNIFORGE_DB_PATH. It can open the SQLite DB directly to read/alter every other tool's source, and write anywhere the app user can. One run turns LAN/MCP access into credential + data theft and tampering.
evidence: Benign PoC tool output: {"sees_OMNIFORGE_API_KEY":"test-key", "db_path_env":".../omniforge.db", "db_readable":true, "db_tools":[...], "uid":1000, "parent_cmdline":"...uvicorn app.main:app..."}. runner.py:62 environment = os.environ.copy() passed to subprocess.run (runner.py:80).
suggested_fix: Run scripts with a scrubbed allowlist environment (like _installer_environment in dependencies.py): drop OMNIFORGE_API_KEY and other secrets; give the script no path to the DB; store the DB outside any script-writable/readable location.
exposure_note: LAN: high (secret + full data exfil on any single run). Exposed: critical. Container hardening does NOT mitigate this - it is in-process data/secret theft, not host escape.

title: No Host-header validation enables DNS-rebinding drive-by RCE from any page David visits
failure_scenario: David (on the LAN) visits an attacker web page. The page uses DNS rebinding to make its own hostname resolve to 192.168.0.180:8000. After rebind the fetch('/api/tools', JSON POST) is same-origin, so there is no CORS preflight and the response is readable. The server accepts any Host, so it answers normally. The page creates+runs a tool (SEC-01) and reads back OMNIFORGE_API_KEY and the DB (SEC-02). No LAN foothold or credential needed - only that David browses the web.
evidence: Server returns 200 for arbitrary Host headers (curl -H 'Host: attacker.com' and 'Host: rebind.evil.example:1337' both 200); no TrustedHostMiddleware/add_middleware anywhere (grep). No CORS middleware (OPTIONS /api/tools -> 405, no Access-Control-* on any response), which blocks classic JSON CSRF but not post-rebind same-origin access. App binds 0.0.0.0 (Dockerfile CMD / uvicorn --host 0.0.0.0). Full rebind race not executed (localhost-only test scope); both preconditions proven.
suggested_fix: Add Starlette TrustedHostMiddleware with an explicit allowed_hosts list (the NAS IP/hostname and localhost); reject unknown Host/Origin on state-changing routes. Combine with auth on /api/* (SEC-01).
exposure_note: LAN: high - needs only that the single user browses a malicious page while the service runs; impact is full unauth RCE + key/DB theft. Mitigants that lower probability: attacker must target the exact IP:port and win the rebind race, and browsers increasingly apply Private Network Access checks. Arguably critical given the trivial precondition.

title: MCP bearer key is equivalent to shell; omniforge_create_tool has no approval step
failure_scenario: An LLM client holding the MCP key (or a prompt-injected LLM handed the key) calls tools/call omniforge_create_tool with is_active=true, then tools/call on the new tool. There is no human approval, no sandbox, and the new tool runs immediately, so the LLM obtains in-container RCE and can exfiltrate OMNIFORGE_API_KEY itself (the very key it was given) plus the DB. Overwrite protection (create-only) is irrelevant because creating a brand-new tool suffices.
evidence: Over POST /mcp with Bearer test-key: omniforge_create_tool returned {"ok":true,"is_active":true,"executed":false}; a follow-up tools/call returned {"stolen_api_key":"test-key","db":".../omniforge.db"}. mcp_server.py:118-127 save_tool with no approval; is_active default True (CREATE_SCHEMA line 26); handler.tools() lists active tools immediately.
suggested_fix: Treat tool creation/execution as privileged: require an explicit out-of-band approval (dashboard confirm) before a newly authored tool becomes callable; default is_active=false for MCP-created tools; never expose the server's own OMNIFORGE_API_KEY to scripts (SEC-02).
exposure_note: LAN: high. The MCP key is the one credential in the system yet confers full code execution and self-leaks; if that key reaches an untrusted/injected model, game over. Exposed: critical.

title: Cross-tool dependency-cache poisoning via writable, script-reachable OMNIFORGE_LIB_ROOT
failure_scenario: A script runs as the same uid that owns OMNIFORGE_LIB_ROOT and knows its path from the inherited env. It writes a malicious module (plus a .complete marker) into another tool's per-tool/per-language/per-requirements-hash cache dir, or overwrites a module in an already-populated cache. Because each tool runs with its cache dir prepended to PYTHONPATH/NODE_PATH (runner.py:64-66), the victim tool imports the planted code on its next run. The poisoning persists in the named volume (omniforge_lib) across restarts.
evidence: Benign PoC tool wrote /.../lib/POC_CACHE_POISON.txt and listed the dir. OMNIFORGE_LIB_ROOT is exported into the script env (confirmed by SEC-02 PoC). Install layout documented as OMNIFORGE_LIB_ROOT/<tool-id-hash>/<lang>/<reqs-hash>.
suggested_fix: Keep OMNIFORGE_LIB_ROOT out of the script environment and make per-tool cache dirs read-only to the executing script (e.g. install as a different uid, mount caches read-only into the run, or copy the needed cache into a throwaway per-run dir).
exposure_note: LAN: medium - integrity break that persists across runs and container restarts, turning one tool compromise into silent compromise of others. Extends the documented shared-subprocess limitation into persistence.

title: No per-script resource limits: memory cap unenforced, no PID cap, no output cap, orphan children survive timeout
failure_scenario: A tool can exhaust the single-worker server: allocate unbounded memory (OMNIFORGE_MAX_SCRIPT_MEMORY_MB is declared but never applied), print unbounded stdout (captured fully into RAM then into the HTTP response), fork, or spawn a detached child that outlives the configured timeout. The runner's subprocess.run timeout kills only the direct child; detached grandchildren keep running.
evidence: PoC /proc/self/limits: Max address space unlimited, Max resident unlimited, Max cpu time unlimited (no setrlimit). A tool printing 20 MiB returned 20,971,595 bytes untruncated. A detached child (start_new_session) wrote its marker 3s after the script returned (reparented ppid=1). runner.py uses capture_output=True (line 83), timeout=MAX_TIMEOUT_MS/1000+15 (line 85), no preexec_fn/rlimits, no process-group kill.
suggested_fix: Apply setrlimit (RLIMIT_AS, RLIMIT_NPROC, RLIMIT_CPU, RLIMIT_FSIZE) via preexec_fn; run each script in its own process group/session and kill the whole group on timeout; cap captured stdout/stderr size.
exposure_note: LAN: medium (single user can DoS their own box; container CPU/RAM/PID limits on the NAS bound total damage to the container but not individual-script output/orphans). Depends on container hardening - the WSL test host had no such limits. Exposed: higher (anonymous DoS).

title: Rate limiting absent (slowapi dependency never wired) and no request body size limit
failure_scenario: Nothing throttles requests, so the optional MCP bearer key can be brute-forced without lockout, and large bodies are accepted (8 MiB tool code stored without complaint). With no size cap and no concurrency/memory guard, repeated large create/run calls can exhaust memory on the single worker.
evidence: slowapi is in requirements.txt:7 but grep of app/ finds no Limiter/@limiter/middleware - it is unused. /api/config reports connection_tracking:false. POST /api/tools with an ~8 MiB code field returned 200. No Content-Length/body-size rejection observed.
suggested_fix: Actually wire slowapi (or reverse-proxy rate limits) on /mcp and /api/*; enforce a max request body size; add a small fixed delay/lockout on failed key checks.
exposure_note: LAN: low (single trusted user). Exposed: medium - unthrottled brute force of the only credential plus easy memory DoS.

title: API key compared with non-constant-time ==
failure_scenario: _check_api_key does `token == API_KEY`, a short-circuiting comparison. In principle a remote attacker could use response-timing to recover the key byte by byte; in practice network jitter on a LAN makes this impractical.
evidence: app/main.py:222 `return token == API_KEY` (no hmac.compare_digest). Also note the key is read once into a module global.
suggested_fix: Use hmac.compare_digest(token, API_KEY) for the comparison.
exposure_note: LAN: low/informational (timing side-channel over LAN is noisy). Exposed: low-medium, especially combined with no rate limiting (SEC-07).

title: Empty default key disables MCP auth; public image + 0.0.0.0 bind makes an unconfigured deploy fully open
failure_scenario: If OMNIFORGE_API_KEY is unset/empty, _check_api_key returns True for everyone, so even the one gated route (POST /mcp) is open. The public image (dbzocchi/omniforge:latest) and docker-compose default `${OMNIFORGE_API_KEY:-}` both leave it empty, and the app binds 0.0.0.0, so a copy-paste deployment with no key is unauthenticated RCE (SEC-01 + open MCP) on whatever network it lands on.
evidence: main.py:216 `if not API_KEY: return True`; API_KEY default '' (main.py:32). docker-compose.yml OMNIFORGE_API_KEY: ${OMNIFORGE_API_KEY:-}. .env.example ships OMNIFORGE_API_KEY=change-me. Docker Hub repo dbzocchi/omniforge is_private:false, pull_count 182. (David's own instance DOES set the key - verified auth_enabled:true.)
suggested_fix: Fail closed: refuse to start (or bind only to 127.0.0.1) when no key is set; document that empty = open; avoid shipping a guessable placeholder.
exposure_note: LAN (David, key set): not currently triggered. Risk is to anyone who pulls the public image and runs it without setting the key - then fully open.

title: No security headers on the dashboard (no CSP, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, HSTS)
failure_scenario: The dashboard HTML is served with only Cache-Control. With no X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors it is framable (clickjacking), and with no CSP any future stored/DOM XSS would be unmitigated and could script the unauthenticated API. No XSS sink exists today (see notes), so this is latent.
evidence: curl -D- / shows only cache-control:no-store, content-type; no CSP/X-Frame-Options/Referrer-Policy/HSTS. (static assets and /sw.js do set X-Content-Type-Options:nosniff.)
suggested_fix: Add a strict CSP (default-src 'self'; the page uses an inline <script>, so use a nonce), X-Frame-Options: DENY / frame-ancestors 'none', Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, and X-Content-Type-Options on the HTML too.
exposure_note: LAN: low. Exposed: low-medium (defense-in-depth; matters more if any XSS is introduced).

title: GET /mcp is unauthenticated
failure_scenario: GET /mcp returns an SSE stub to anyone with no key check. It only emits a static protocolVersion today, so disclosure is negligible, but it confirms the inconsistent auth model (POST gated, GET not).
evidence: curl GET /mcp with no Authorization -> 200, body `event: initial-connections / data: {"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05"}`. main.py:207 mcp_sse has no _check_api_key.
suggested_fix: Apply the same auth to GET /mcp; or remove the stub until a real SSE transport exists.
exposure_note: LAN: informational. Exposed: low (no sensitive data, but unauth).

title: Minor information exposure via /api/config and validation errors
failure_scenario: /api/config (unauthenticated) returns the exact auth posture (auth_enabled, methods, warnings) that helps an attacker plan. 422 validation responses echo the submitted body back. Neither leaks server secrets or stack traces, so impact is low.
evidence: GET /api/config returns auth_enabled/transport/methods/warnings unauthenticated. POST with text/plain or a JSON array returns 422 with the submitted input echoed (input field). No Python stack traces leaked at the HTTP layer (clean 422/401). Script stderr (tracebacks) IS returned by /run and tools/call by design.
suggested_fix: Gate /api/config behind auth (or trim it); avoid echoing submitted bodies in error detail. Script stderr return is acceptable for a trusted-author tool but should be noted.
